findings.observed: After a before_head_swap crash, registry current head remained absent but one registry ledger head was already present. A later append_registry_event returned success and published a different head. The next read_registry_ledger_head failed with BA11_LEDGER_FORK.
findings.required_fix: Separate candidate/staged ledger objects from published ledger authority, or make the publication rail explicitly distinguish reachable published heads from unreferenced content-addressed candidates. A pre-swap crash must not poison or fork later valid work.
findings.root_cause: commit_transaction writes registry/debt ledger heads and sets into the same directories that _read_persistent_ledger later treats as published authority before the registry head swap. A crash before_head_swap leaves an unreferenced candidate head there.
findings.title: Pre-swap staging pollutes the authoritative ledger namespace

findings.observed: Attempting to build the next governance graph after one committed promotion fails with BA11_AUTHORITY_GRAPH_MISMATCH:promotion_event_count before a second promotion can be represented.
findings.required_fix: RegistryAuthorityGraph must identify the current promotion event by exact event hash / candidate binding, not by requiring it to be the only promotion event in history. Historical PromotionEvents remain valid append-only evidence.
findings.root_cause: _promotion_event requires exactly one PromotionEvent in objects.registry_events, while registry_events simultaneously represent the full append-only ledger used to derive the snapshot and ledger head. A second legitimate candidate/review/approval/promotion cycle therefore produces two historical PromotionEvents and is rejected.
findings.title: The append-only model cannot represent a second valid promotion cycle

findings.observed: storage.py contains head_history writes and predecessor loading for replay, but no read-time validation that the mutable current RegistryHead is the latest published head or that there is no alternative published branch.
findings.required_fix: Add a fail-closed published RegistryHead authority chain. Candidate/staged heads may exist without becoming authority; published heads/commit receipts must form one monotonic chain. Rollback of current to an older valid head and publication from an old base must block.
findings.root_cause: read_head only validates the hash-bound current.json object. It does not verify the published RegistryHead chain, maximum committed generation, a publication receipt chain, or that current.json is the latest authoritative publication.
findings.title: Top-level RegistryHead current pointer has no rollback/fork authority check

findings.observed: 54 acceptance rows map to 50 test functions; two parameterized functions each cover three requirements under the same source function name and suite-level stdout hash.
findings.required_fix: Bind every requirement to an exact pytest node ID (including parameter ID), a collection manifest, and an execution result for that node. The verifier must reject missing, duplicate, uncollected or unexecuted node IDs.
findings.root_cause: The verifier resolves a source function name globally and a command receipt, but does not prove that each requirement maps to one exact collected/executed pytest node ID. Parameterized tests are reused for multiple requirement rows.
findings.title: Acceptance evidence is not uniquely bound to concrete pytest node IDs
